text:
jin: FYI saw a noisy eviction spike in ap-southeast1a around 03:42 UTC. Looks like a topologySpreadConstraint + fractional GPU jobs scatter across racks, then TOR (top-of-rack) egress hits a knob and kubelet evicts pods with "network pressure".

rachel: Wait, topologySpreadConstraint is intentionally spreading tiny training pods across zones/racks to avoid co-tenancy. That should be fine unless NIC or switch is the bottleneck.

omar: Can you paste events + any node labels? Might be that the scheduler is spreading but not considering tor-egress headroom label we added last quarter.

jin: Pasting filtered events from one thread: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason       Age   From               Message
  ----     ------       ----  ----               -------
  Warning  Evicted      2m    kubelet            Pod evicted: resource pressure: nodefs
  Warning  Evicted      2m    kubelet            Pod evicted: resource pressure: NIC egress
  Normal   Scheduled    1m    kubescheduler      Successfully assigned default/light-train-xyz to n3-rack7-node03
  Warning  FailedSync   1m    kubelet            Error syncing pod, skipping: failed to setup network: TOR egress limit exceeded
```

samir: nodefs + NIC egress both? nodefs probably red herring from ephemeral docker layer writes. The consistent signal is TOR egress.

rachel: Which scheduling constraints are these pods using? Are they requesting fractional GPUs via device-plugin or requesting whole GPU?

jin: They request 0.25 GPU (we do fractional via MIG-like virtual GPUs). Scheduler treats that as scalar resource "gpu.milli" in our predicate. Spread constraints still apply, so many pods land on different racks.

omar: That explains scatter. MIG-like packing increases fragmentation across racks -> more TOR egress because training checkpoints and data pulls are cross-rack.

ops-bot: Alert: ap-southeast1 TOR egress saturation detected (rack7, rack11). Auto-scaling suppressed due to capacity limits.

rachel: Short-term mitigation: prefer binpacking of fractional-GPU pods to minimize rack-span when there is high egress. Two levers: 1) a scheduling weight that prefers same-rack placement (rackAffinity) 2) an admission limit on concurrent fractional-GPU pods per rack.

samir: I can push a small scheduler plugin that adds a rack-affinity score for gpu.milli pods. Canary it in ap-southeast1 for 1 hour.

jin: Also recommend throttling simultaneous starts from the CI job runner group; they create bursty starts that amplify the egress spike.

omar: Ops action: add a temporary cluster-level taint 'rack-egress-saturated=true:NoSchedule' for the two racks hardest hit, and drain a few nodes to shift heavy egress workloads to beefier racks. That should give breathing room.

rachel: For medium-term: we should teach autoscaler to prefer beefier NIC-per-GPU flavors when fractional packing is heavy. Also add a headroom metric for TOR egress into scoring.

ops-bot: Incident timeline note: spike started 03:42 UTC, mitigation (rack taint) applied 03:58 UTC, evictions reduced 70% by 04:10 UTC.

samir: I'll open the canary PR for the scheduler affinity: https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler/pulls/2521. Plan: score +100 for nodes in same rack that already host fractional-GPU pods from same deployment.

jin: Nice. Action items: samir canary PR +1h, omar do rack-level cordon/drain for two racks, rachel propose flavor changes to autoscaler, jin throttle CI starts (coord with ci-team). Post postmortem with a graph of rack egress vs fraction-gpu pod starts.

omar: One more note: long-term we should evaluate packing fractional GPUs into multi-GPU nodes with NVLink for distributed training instead of scattering MIGs across racks. That will change cost math but reduce tail latency and network egress.

rachel: Agreed. TL;DR: fractional GPU scatter + topologySpread => TOR egress saturation => eviction cascade. Short-term: rack-affinity canary + cordon two racks. Medium: autoscaler flavor + start-rate limits. Long: topology-aware fractional binpacking (and maybe NVLink-aware placements). :white_check_mark:
